summary:
The ACES Act of 2025 (Public Law 119-32) directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to enter into an agreement with the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine to conduct a study on the prevalence and mortality of cancer among individuals who served as active duty aircrew in the Armed Forces. 

Section 2(a) requires the Secretary, not later than 30 days after the date of enactment, to seek to enter into an agreement with the National Academies. The Secretary must finalize the agreement not later than 60 days after entering negotiations. If the Secretary fails to meet this deadline, the Secretary must submit a report to the Committee on Veterans' Affairs of the Senate and the Committee on Veterans' Affairs of the House of Representatives explaining the failure and estimating the finalization date, and must provide subsequent progress briefings not less frequently than once every 60 days.

Section 2(b) specifies the study's scope. The National Academies must identify exposures associated with the military occupations of covered individuals, including chemicals, compounds, agents, and other phenomena. The study must review literature to determine associations between these exposures and overall cancer morbidity and mortality, as well as the incidence or prevalence of specific enumerated cancers (brain, colon and rectal, kidney, lung, melanoma skin, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, pancreatic, prostate, testicular, thyroid, and urinary bladder cancers), and other cancers as determined appropriate by the Secretary in consultation with the National Academies. The study must also determine the prevalence and mortality from these cancers among covered individuals using available data sources, which may include databases of the Department of Veterans Affairs, the Department of Defense, and the individual Services; the national death index maintained by the National Center for Health Statistics; and the study conducted under section 750 of the William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021 (Public Law 116-283).

Section 2(c) requires the National Academies to submit a report containing the study results to the Secretary and the House and Senate Committees on Veterans' Affairs upon the study's conclusion. 

Section 2(d) defines a "covered individual" as an individual who served on active duty in the Army, Navy, Air Force, or Marine Corps as an aircrew member of a fixed-wing aircraft, including pilots, navigators, weapons systems operators, aircraft system operators, or any other crew member who regularly flew in a fixed-wing aircraft. The Act was approved on August 14, 2025.
